title: Few lovers of the cross (II.11)
hookLine: many follow Jesus to the breaking of bread, few to the cup
tomorrow: can carrying something heavy ever make it lighter?

lines: A FULL TABLE, A SLEEPING GARDEN.
cards: The party's over. The music's off, cups are everywhere, and the room that held a crowd now holds three people with trash bags. Every gathering has that crew, the ones still there when the fun has left, folding the chairs.
The Imitation noticed the same split in Jesus's own story. There's a long table where bread is broken and every seat is taken.
Later that night, in the garden of Gethsemane, he prays that a cup might pass from him, and his friends fall asleep.

teach.h: MANY AT THE TABLE, FEW AT THE FAST.
teach.b: Chapter eleven of book two lays it out in pairs. Jesus has many lovers of his heavenly kingdom, it says, but few who carry his cross. Many want comfort; few want trouble.
Many will sit at his table; few will fast with him.

Then the line the day is built on: many follow him as far as the breaking of bread, few as far as drinking the cup of his passion. Many admire the miracles; few follow him into the shame of the cross.
The chapter isn't sneering at anyone.
It's a mirror, and the reader is meant to look into it, not at the neighbor. Then the turn, and it's a hard one.
Those who love Jesus for himself, the chapter says, bless him in trouble as much as in the highest joy, and even if he never gave them comfort, they would still praise him and give thanks.

That's the test of love it cares about: not how you show up to the feast, but whether you stay for the garden. In an ordinary week that can look small, almost invisible. The bus ride home after a loss.
The friend who's still crying after everyone else has gone home. The table is easy to find. The cup is where friends are counted.

how: Catholics speak of offering up a hardship, uniting it with Christ's passion, and many pray the Sorrowful Mysteries of the rosary, which begin with the agony in the garden.

games.q: what does “few lovers of the cross” mean?
o: few people like to wear a crucifix
few stay with Jesus when suffering comes
few saints were ever asked to suffer

games.q: the table and the cup — tap the pairs.

s: loving the cross means wanting to suffer
the chapter is about staying when trouble comes, loving Jesus for himself and not only for comfort.
the chapter sets the breaking of bread beside the cup of the passion
many follow to the bread, it says; few to the cup.
the Imitation says almost nobody loves Jesus
it says many love him while things go well; few follow him to the cup.

games.q: a friend's grandmother has died. everyone came to the funeral lunch; a week later, the texts have stopped. what does chapter eleven point toward?
o: check in now, when fewer people are still around.
wait for her to reach out when she's ready.
send flowers at the next holiday instead.
games.why: many come to the table; few stay for the cup. the quiet week after is where friends are counted.

practice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one hard thing you're in the middle of: a worry, an ache, a waiting. Instead of hurrying out of it, stay beside it for the sit, breathing slowly, the way a friend keeps watch through a long night.
If you pray, you can offer it as a small share of his cup.

wordCard.voice: Few lovers of the cross. The Imitation's mirror: many follow Jesus to the breaking of bread, few to the cup of his passion.

orig.note: Latin, from the Imitation II.11: the cup of the passion, which few follow Jesus to drink.

carryVoice: Keep this one: to the cup, where the friends who stay get counted, quietly. Rest easy tonight.
